summary: Register-only lookout at 385 m in Sudbury District; the location is the author's estimate and no source gives its build, staffing or site status.

evidence.supports: Register location: Road 1002, Unorganized North Sudbury, Sudbury District
evidence.quote: Road 1002, Unorganized North Sudbury, Sudbury District, Northeastern Ontario, Ontario, Canada

evidence.supports: Location is the register author's estimate, worked out from topographic maps and geological surveys
evidence.quote: This is the best I can do, I think, using topographic maps and geological surveys, that this is the right place.

evidence.supports: The register author says the location could be wrong
evidence.quote: I still could be wrong, though.

evidence.supports: Most Ontario towers erected between the 1920s and the 1950s
evidence.quote: Most of the towers were erected between the 1920's and the 1950's when forest fire protection was in it's heyday.

evidence.supports: Towers came under the Department of Lands and Forests, which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: From the 1960s aerial spotting and fire-fighting crews took over the towers' work
evidence.quote: As the 1960's progressed the towers were in use less and less as aerial fire spotting and fire fighting crews took over.

evidence.supports: Government did not want lawsuits over people hurt climbing unmanned towers
evidence.quote: The government decided that they didn't want any lawsuits on their hands in case careless citizens climbed the unmanned towers and were injured in the process.

evidence.supports: Many towers were destroyed after the decision
evidence.quote: The decision then went through to have many destroyed.

sources.title: Ontario's Fire Tower Lookouts: Preserving Their History

notes_for_editor: Register-only record: Firelookout.ca gives no build year, tower type, structure height, status or access, and its location is the author's own best estimate ('I still could be wrong, though'). Coordinates are therefore approximate. Two Ontario fire-tower sources were checked for this tower by name and were silent: the Forest History Society of Ontario journal (spring 2013) and the Sudbury News 'Sentinels of the forest' article (Jan 2021); the Foleyet Wikipedia page mentions no tower. Story's general Ontario context is from the Ontario Fire Tower Lookouts site, not from anything specific to this tower. Needs a second source before any build, staffing or status claim. No photos found.
